newsitem.title: ANGOLA: ICRC begins cutting back operations in Angola.
newsitem.headline: ICRC begins cutting back operations in Angola.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross has halted aid programmes in Angola ahead of a gradual pullout from the country now moving from 20 years of civil war to peace.

ICRC chief in Angola Michel Dufour told Reuters at the weekend that the organisation, which offered relief to thousands of victims of the country's civil war, would now begin handing over some of its programmes to the government.

"We terminated all assistance programmes by the end of December 1996 and we shall be handing over water and medical programmes to authorities or to other NGOs (non-governmental organisations)," Dufour said.
He said the ICRC would cut expatriate staff to 20 from 65 in 1997.
"We decided to accompany the peace process with rehabilitation programmes. Now it is time we should enter into the phase of reconstruction," Dufour said.

Among ICRC's rehabilitation programmes has been a seed distribution project to communities living in government and former rebel UNITA areas around the agricultural-rich central highland towns of Huambo, Kuito and Bailundo.
The ICRC, which entered Angola in 1975, set up one of the biggest programmes in the country for the manufacture of artificial limbs for an estimated 30,000 amputees.
Diana, Britain's Princess of Wales, visited the orthopaedic centre in Huambo last week as part of a tour to support a British Red Cross campaign to ban landmines.
Dufour said the ICRC would participate in programmes to assist with the integration of government and UNITA forces into a single army.
"After integration we will participate in teaching soldiers general behaviour rules in line with international law," he said.

Nine top UNITA generals have already been officially integrated into a new Angolan Armed Forces (FAA). The United Nations, helping to implement a peace pact, is overseeing the integration of 26,300 UNITA soldiers in the FAA.
